# Architecture — Perry > Written by: agent · Confirmed by: user (§1, §3 Forbidden, §5 versions, §6, §7) > Version: v1 > Last reviewed: 2026-09-15 > Hard cap: ≤ 500 lines. It has two readers — the user in one sitting, and every > agent that is dispatched against it — and the second one pays for it per turn. > Overflow → split per-§ to `architecture/sections/§-.md`. **This file existing is what makes it binding.** There is no draft state: a document that describes the system is the description, and a change that contradicts a section stops and asks the user (DESIGN-017 decisions 2 and 4). ## §1. Mission & scope Perry is a project office for solo and small projects, run by agents and read by one human. It keeps goals, work and decisions as files in the project's own repository, and it computes every number it reports rather than eyeballing it. It runs as a **skill** on three hosts — Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex CLI — with no install step and no service. The `bin/` tools are stdlib-only Python 3 and POSIX-ish bash, invoked by the skill's own procedures. It deliberately does **not**: run unattended (every write is a command an agent was asked to make), judge what a document means in code (that is an agent's job, `DESIGN-014`), or hold state outside the project it is pointed at (`ADR-002` — there is no cross-project registry). ## §2. Components ### `bin/` — the deterministic tools - **Purpose**: read and write project state. Twenty-one executables plus three shared libraries; `perry-kernel` is the `kernel/` CLI below. - **Owns**: every write to a canonical store, every computed number the standup prints, the argument contract those calls are made through, and the **next-step recommendation**: `perry-state --section next` evaluates the declared rule table `reference/next-rules.json` over the payload it already computes, so the same state gives the same recommendation. The move is the user's decision, `perry/design/DESIGN-020-guided-planning.md § 9`, the 2026-09-15 entry, confirmed by the user in session. - **Doesn't own**: the rules, which are declared in `reference/`, or the procedure around a recommendation — when to show it and what to ask the user are the `SKILL.md` files'. These tools execute, compute and refuse. - **Module document**: [`bin/ARCHITECTURE.md`](bin/ARCHITECTURE.md) ### `kernel/` — the PMO kernel (DESIGN-023) - **Purpose**: hold a project's structured state in one store per project anchor and answer for it through one CLI, JSON in and JSON out. Built by DESIGN-023 § 6 row B, behind `bin/perry-kernel`; `bin/` stays the live writer until each lane cuts over. - **Owns**: the store (`/perry/.db`, or `/.perry/perry.db` outside git) and its deterministic export under `/export/`; eight concepts and at most twelve command groups; every structural check a guard can decide without reading for meaning; and the derived fields `startable`, `blocked_by`, a metric's `met` and `fraction`, and `rollup`. - **Doesn't own**: the method. Item types, states, fields and guards are the process template, which the skill ships as data under `templates/process/`. The kernel reads no markdown, runs no command, and names no skill path or template-declared name. - **Module document**: [`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md`](kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md) ### `release/` — Perry product versions and releases - **Purpose**: maintain Perry's own product versions and verified release updates. - **Owns**: typed release records, deterministic VERSION/CHANGELOG projections, integration checks and explicit publication of an exact tested commit. - **Doesn't own**: the versions or state of projects managed by Perry, the meaning of authored change notes, or the user's decision to raise a major version. - **Procedure**: [`release/README.md`](release/README.md). ### `viewer/parsers.py` — the one reader - **Purpose**: parse every state file. 5,228 lines, one implementation. - **Owns**: `OKR.md`, phase, linkage, config and architecture parsing, and the store readers the read payloads answer from — a `BOARD.md` a project still holds is parsed only for the import verbs (TASK-262 round 4b); the project-root and state-root resolution, and the `installed` predicate, both `bin/` and the skill read through. - **Doesn't own**: writing. A second parser is the defect this repository has shipped twice; `NN-1` below is that rule. ### `schema/` — the declared shape - **Purpose**: `state-schema.json` (107KB) declares every file, heading, table, enum, store and claim. Eight contract pages publish the payloads outside consumers read; `next-contract.md` is the eighth. - **Owns**: what a file must look like, and what a payload promises. - **Doesn't own**: how a tool reaches that shape. ### `SKILL.md` + `goals/` `work/` `decide/` — the lanes - **Purpose**: the router (tier 0, read on every invocation; its byte cap is `tests/test_router_budget.py`'s) and three lane files loaded on demand. - **Owns**: procedure — what an agent does, in what order, and when it stops to ask the user. A lane **renders** the next step `perry-state --section next` returns: **in a standup's TL;DR and in its next-step position** it does not add, drop or reorder a recommendation, and it may add one line marked as its own note (`perry/design/DESIGN-020-guided-planning.md § 9`, the 2026-09-15 entry, confirmed by the user in session). - **Outside that rule**, and still the lane's own to write: a procedural step inside a subcommand's instructions ("read this, then run that"); the remediation a refusal names ("no current phase — run `plan-phase` first"); bootstrap and first-run prompts; and a hint in a rendered dashboard row. First-time setup is the largest of them: on a directory with no Perry state `R-setup` recommends only `/perry`, and the order setup recommends after that is the router's own (`reference/first-run.md § The recommended order for a new project`, which the router's first-time setup points to). The rule is about the one position the next block owns, not about naming a command. - **Doesn't own**: any number, or which step to recommend. Every figure a lane prints comes from a `bin/` call, and so does the recommendation. ### `modes/`, `packs/`, `reference/`, `templates/` - **Purpose**: the vocabulary a project can declare (four work modes), the domain pack (`software-ops`, which is where this discipline is defined), tier-1 reference pages loaded on demand, and the scaffolds a new project gets. `reference/` also holds `next-rules.json`, the rule table `bin/perry-state` evaluates for the next step, and `next.md`, which explains each rule. - **Owns**: per-project variation. A track's mode, a pack's glossary. The next-step rules, declared as data that `bin/` evaluates. ### `tests/` — 163 modules - **Purpose**: the contract, executable. Includes `tests/tree_guard.py`, which fails the suite if a run changed the checkout it ran in. - **Owns**: whether a claim in this repository is true. ### `perry/` and `.perry/` — this project's own state - **Purpose**: Perry's state root and anchor. Perry runs its own office in its own repository. ## §3. Boundaries & dependencies ```mermaid flowchart TD User([the one human]) -->|reads, decides| Lanes Lanes["SKILL.md · goals / work / decide
procedure only"] -->|invokes| Bin Bin["bin/ — 21 tools
compute and write"] -->|imports| Parsers["viewer/parsers.py
the one reader"] Bin -->|imports| Lib["bin/lib · perry_store · perry_md_store"] Bin -->|validates against| Schema["schema/state-schema.json"] Parsers -->|reads| State[("perry/ · .perry/
stores and projections")] Bin -->|writes| State Tests["tests/ — 163 modules"] -.asserts.-> Bin Tests -.asserts.-> Parsers Tests -.asserts.-> Schema Outside([aiMark and other consumers]) -->|published payloads| Contracts["schema/*-contract.md"] Contracts -.described by.-> Bin ``` Allowed directions: lanes → tools → libraries → state. Tools import `parsers`; `parsers` imports nothing from `bin/`. Forbidden, and each one has cost this project something: - **A second reader of any state file.** `bin/` never re-implements a parse. - **A lane computing a number.** If a figure is not in a payload, the tool grows the field; the procedure does not count rows. - **A tool reaching another project.** Roots come from `--root`, then `$PERRY_PROJECT`, then the walk up — `ADR-002`, and `bin/lib § resolve_project_root` is the one implementation. **Sunset (proposed, DESIGN-023)**: this becomes false at DESIGN-023 § 6 row H. The kernel's resolver (`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.7, NN-K5) is the second implementation DESIGN-023 introduces. It walks in the same order as `bin/lib § resolve_project_root` with a different predicate — it stops at the first `.perry/`, not the first installed project — and it refuses (`anchor_not_found`) where `bin/lib` falls back to the working directory or takes a `--root` or `$PERRY_PROJECT` that holds no `.perry/`. `kernel/tests/test_resolver_agreement.py` pins those four differences on both sides and shows the two agree on a shared set of fixture roots. The copies that already exist are unchanged and go at row H: `bin/perry-state § resolve_root`, `viewer/parsers.py § _resolve_project_root`, the flag/env/cwd lines in `perry-decide`, `perry-task`, `perry-knowledge`, `perry-state-cost`, `perry-context-budget` and `perry-explain`, `bin/perry-churn § detect_perry`, which walks up to the first `.perry/`, stops at the git top level, and takes no `--root` and no environment variable, and `perry-lint`, which reads no `$PERRY_PROJECT` at any of its nine sites: one, the default lint, walks, and eight per-mode branches (`--claims`, `--verification`, `--summaries`, `--glossary`, `--reviews`, `--knowledge`, `--provenance`, `--specs`) take `--root` or else the cwd, with no walk. - **An agent writing `ARCHITECTURE.md`.** This file is the user's. ## §4. Data flow **The store is truth; the markdown is a projection of it** (`ADR-007`). Every mutating command writes the record first. The board is not a file: `perry-tasks board` prints it from the stores. A `BOARD.md` a project still holds is retired — no write or reader uses it, only the `--from-board` imports read it, and every tool that sees it says to import and then delete it (TASK-262 rounds 4a and 4b). ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph write["a mutating command"] direction TB A["perry-task <verb>"] --> B["tasks.jsonl
the record"] B --> C["journal/<YYYY-MM>/<day>.md
the history line"] B --> E[".perry/events.jsonl
derived, disposable"] end B -.->|"(1) and (2) are one
recoverable transaction"| C C -.->|"(3) may fail alone
— reported, not silent"| E ``` Eight stores exist, one verdict line each in `perry-lint`'s census: `tasks.jsonl`, `risks.jsonl`, `intake.jsonl`, `asks.jsonl`, `cadence.jsonl`, `okr.jsonl`, `linkage.jsonl`, `.perry/config.jsonl`. `cadence.jsonl` is the newest (TASK-237 deliverable 3b). The read path is the mirror image and has one entry point: ```mermaid flowchart LR State[("stores + projections")] --> P["viewer/parsers.py"] P --> S["perry-state"] S -->|"--compact ≈ 11KB"| Standup["the standup, every session"] S -->|"--section <name>"| Detail["one key, in full"] S -->|"--section next --lane / --after"| Next["the next block,
narrowed"] S -->|"--json ≈ 174KB"| Whole["the whole payload"] T["perry-task list --json"] -->|"contract 2.4, bounded"| Outside([aiMark]) ``` `--section next` is the one section that is not always the payload's key as it stands. With `--lane` or `--after` it prints the block evaluated again over only that lane's or that subcommand's rules, plus the overlays (TASK-442). ## §5. Contracts ### Contract: `bin/` → an agent (the argument surface) - **Input**: ` [flags]`. Each tool declares its surface in `SURFACE`; the parser is driven by that declaration. - **Output**: exit 0 read or written · 1 refused, reason printed · 2 bad invocation · 3 the bytes match and the store did not produce them. These two bullets describe the other `bin/` tools: `bin/perry-kernel` has no `SURFACE` (`describe` is its surface), and its exit 3 is an internal fault (`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.1). - **Invariant on the tool**: a flag reaches only the subcommands that declare it. Accepted-and-dropped is a defect (`DESIGN-016` goal 12). - **Invariant on the caller**: a refusal is an outcome, not a failure. Do not fall back to editing the file by hand. ### Contract: `perry-task list --json` → outside consumers - `schema/task-list-contract.md`, version **2.4** (confirmed by the user 2026-09-15; 2.2 adds `installed`, 2.3 narrows it to a store with `.perry/` beside it, 2.4 reads no `BOARD.md` a project still holds — TASK-262 round 4b). `tasks[]` is bounded at 200 rows by default; `bound.open_total` carries the project's figure. - **Error mode**: a refusal is JSON on stdout, not prose on stderr. ### Contract: `perry-state --json` / `--compact` → the standup - `--compact` is a strict projection of `--json`, declared once in `perry-state § COMPACT` and asserted against the full payload by test. ### Contract: the schema → both sides - `perry-lint --templates` fails when a shipped template drifts from `state-schema.json`. That check is what keeps the standup from breaking silently. ## §6. Non-negotiables ### NN-1 — One reader per state file - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: exactly one implementation parses any given state file, and it lives in `viewer/parsers.py`. A `bin/` tool that needs a fact imports it. - **Rationale**: two parsers of `BOARD.md` disagreed in production twice, and the disagreement was invisible until a round-trip test one project later. - **Check**: `grep -rn "def parse_" bin/ | grep -v perry_store | grep -v _md_store` - **Known exceptions**: - `bin/perry-context-budget` reads one key (`session_context_ceiling`) of `.perry/config.jsonl` directly, because it must work outside a Perry project (USER-971, 2026-09-18). - `release/manage.py` reads `phase/CURRENT` at two git refs with its own "no phase" set: the pointer reader in `viewer/parsers.py` serves a working tree, and `release/` does not import `viewer/` (USER-981, 2026-09-21). - **Sunset (proposed, DESIGN-023)**: becomes false at DESIGN-023 § 6 row H, when `bin/`, the state readers in `viewer/parsers.py` and the state files they read are deleted, and structured state lives only in the kernel's store, read and written through the kernel CLI. Until row H it holds for everything `bin/` still reads. Its successor is `kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 3: nothing but the kernel opens the store, and only `export`, to decide `unchanged`, and `import` read the export. ### NN-2 — The store is truth; the projection is rendered - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: a mutating command writes the record first. Every reading of it — a payload and `perry-tasks board` — is derived from the record. No command reads, renders or creates a board file; a `BOARD.md` a project still holds is retired, is read only by the import verbs that upgrade the project, and every tool that sees one says it can be deleted. A projection edited by hand is not absorbed: the store is what every reading reports. - **Rationale**: `ADR-007`. Absorbing a hand edit destroys the canonical value; overwriting it destroys the human's intent. Both must be visible. - **Sunset (proposed, DESIGN-023)**: becomes false at DESIGN-023 § 6 row H, when `perry-tasks board`, the `BOARD.md` import verbs and every projection are deleted with `bin/`. The store stays the truth, and nothing is projected from it: readings come from kernel `query`, and the only file derived from the store is the export, which only `export`, to decide `unchanged`, and `import` read (`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.8). ### NN-3 — A write that cannot do what it claims refuses - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: no command reports a write it did not perform. A render that cannot place every stored record exits non-zero and names what it could not place. - **Rationale**: `DESIGN-016 § 1.5`. The documented recovery command reported `rendered … from 399 stored record(s)`, exit 0, having restored none of 151 deleted rows. ### NN-4 — Deterministic tools decide nothing about meaning - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: `bin/` makes only mechanical judgements. Whether a summary reads like prose, whether a spec's scope is adequate, whether an ADR applies — all belong to an agent or the user. - **Rationale**: `DESIGN-014`. Five rounds of regex lost to a full stop. - **Known exceptions**: `perry-codex-preflight` shells out to `codex exec` to check the CLI is alive. It judges nothing; it pings. ### NN-5 — The suite never writes into the tree it runs in - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: every test writes to a temporary root. `tests/tree_guard.py` runs on every exit path and fails the suite otherwise. - **Rationale**: an un-rooted `perry-task` call once discharged real board rows on every run for months, invisibly, because the sweep is idempotent. ### NN-6 — An agent may describe this file, and may not decide it - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: an agent writes and rewrites the descriptive sections (§2, §4, §5's shapes, §8) freely. It may ADD to §6 and §7, marked `proposed`, and may delete from neither. Changing §1, a `Forbidden` line in §3, a contract version in §5, or a confirmed rule in §6 is a question for the user, asked before the change lands. - **Rationale**: the agent doing the typing is what makes this document affordable, and the agent being unable to overrule it is what keeps it from becoming a mirror. A description follows the code and can refuse nothing; this file has to be able to refuse. DESIGN-017 carries the argument. ## §7. Open questions - **OQ-1 — The schema anchors this file in the wrong place.** *Closed 2026-09-21 (USER-987).* TASK-451 (DESIGN-017 A1, main 6d471770) anchors `ARCHITECTURE.md` at the code root in `schema/state-schema.json`; TASK-452 (A2, main 5d661ec6) makes `perry-state` read and cap-check it there, and `--section architecture` reports `exists: true` on this repository. `perry-diagnose`'s ownership scan, the last reader that ignored the code anchor, was fixed by TASK-477 (main a2a12a8f). The text below is the question as it stood. ANSWERED for where it lives, open for the fix. `schema/state-schema.json § files[id=architecture]` and `§ claims` both anchor `ARCHITECTURE.md` at the STATE root; `packs/software-ops/architecture.md` says "at the project root". The user settled the question on 2026-09-09: an architecture document describes code, so it lives at the code root, and `perry/` holds runtime state only. That makes the schema's `anchor: state` the defect — and while it stands, `perry-state --section architecture` reports `exists: false` on a project that has one. Note `.perry/config.jsonl` already separates `pmo_repo_path` from `code_repo_path`, so the resolution rule has somewhere to read from. No row is open for this yet. - **OQ-2 — What is the module document's contract?** This file links `bin/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and nothing yet declares its shape, its cap, its owner, or what happens when it drifts from the code beside it. *Partly answered 2026-09-21 (USER-978):* a component §2 declares no module document for has none — an architecture reviewer does not count its absence as missing context. Shape, cap, owner and drift stay open. - **OQ-3 — Should `perry-lint` check mermaid?** `perry-state` already counts fenced mermaid blocks (`mermaid_count`) and nothing consumes the number. - **OQ-4 — May `--compact` be accepted with `--section next`?** *Proposed* (TASK-442). `DESIGN-020 § 5.4`'s closing step runs `perry-state --section next --after --compact`, and `perry-state` refuses `--compact` together with `--section`. `TASK-443` builds that step and needs one of the two to give way. - **OQ-5 — Should the contract registry recognise a family that is not `/list`?** *Proposed* (TASK-442). `perry-next/1.0` is one object, not a list. `tests/contract_key_parity.py § CONTRACT_ID` matches only a three-part id, so the parity baseline keys `schema/next-contract.md` by its path, and two registry tests had their `/list` assumption widened to take the page at all. - **OQ-6 — May `--section ` print something other than the payload's key?** *Proposed* (TASK-442). §4 describes a section as one key in full. `--section next` with `--lane` or `--after` prints a block evaluated over fewer rules, which is not what `--json` carries under `next`. - **OQ-7 — Does the phase heartbeat survive the move to `--section next`?** *Proposed* (TASK-442). `goals/SKILL.md` prompted a phase snapshot after `phase_heartbeat_days`. That prompt is now the rule `R-phase-heartbeat`, but no value in `perry-state`'s payload dates the last snapshot, so the rule reports its fact unknown and never fires. Keeping it needs `perry-state` to compute that date; dropping it means deleting the rule. - **OQ-8 — What covers the lane lines that name a command with no rule behind them?** *Proposed* (TASK-442). Two kinds are marked and waiting. **After a subcommand**: `goals/SKILL.md`'s `score-phase` row and `goals/reference/phases.md` step 9, both naming `plan-phase`. They are the proactive closing step `TASK-443` builds; when it ships it renders `--after score-phase` and the two lines go. **In a standup's next-step position**: an ADR whose sunset date has passed and the old-style `DECISIONS.md` migration, both in `decide/reference/decisions.md`, and the undigested `inputs/` and stale-digest counts in `work/reference/digests.md`. `reference/next-rules.json` has a rule for none of the four, and **the reason is the bound, not a missing fact**: `DESIGN-020 § 5.3`'s table is what `TASK-442` was bounded to and names none of them, so each is a later row's work. Two of the four already have their fact — `decisions.expired_sunsets` for the sunset, and `operations.inputs` with `operations.inputs_oldest` and `operations.inputs_oldest_days` for the digests. Stale digests have no count in the payload, only per-card staleness under `roles.cards[].knowledge[]`, and the migration has no fact at all; those two need a fact as well as a rule. *Proposed — partly answered 2026-09-23 (TASK-484):* one of the four now has its rule — the undigested `inputs/` line, through `R-inputs-waiting` over the facts `operations.inputs` and `operations.first_input`, and `work/reference/digests.md` was rewritten to stop saying the opposite. The expired-sunset ADR, the `DECISIONS.md` migration and the stale-digest count stay open, and the sentence above holds for those three. ## §8. Change log - 2026-09-24/26 · v1 · TASK-487, four rounds, and TASK-488, each confirmed by the user (NN-6): §2's `kernel/` entry adds `rollup` (its Owns bullet rewrapped to stay within the cap), says the kernel is built, and `bin/` counts 21 executables; §3's third Forbidden line gains a proposed sunset naming the four resolver differences its test pins and the copies row H removes, `perry-lint`'s nine sites among them (round 4); §2 and the §3 diagram count 21 tools and 163 test modules; §5's `bin/` contract says `perry-kernel` follows kernel §5.1. The clause is marked `proposed` because that is what §6 NN-6 grants an agent for a §7 addition; the two annotations in §7 that are not so marked each name a user id. The question's words are kept, and `work/reference/digests.md`, which said the recommendation stays off the next-step position, was rewritten to match what ships. No other section is edited. The move is the user's decision in `perry/design/DESIGN-020-guided-planning.md § 9`, the 2026-09-15 entry, confirmed by the user in session. `bin/ARCHITECTURE.md § 1` says the same. - §2 `schema/`: eight contract pages. §2 `reference/`: it holds the rule table `bin/` evaluates. - §4's read path names the narrowed `--section next`. - §2's lanes say first-time setup sits outside the next block. - §7 gains five questions marked proposed. The fourth is the phase heartbeat. `goals/SKILL.md`'s heartbeat prompt became the rule `R-phase-heartbeat`, declared with its fact reported unknown, because `perry-state` computes no date for the last snapshot. It sits after `R-review-due`, because DESIGN-020's order has no place for it. The user decided that in session on 2026-09-15, after three review rounds each found a different lane line that names a command legitimately. Five TL;DR examples in the three lanes describe state instead of naming a step, and the `goals` bootstrap prompt says it is outside the rule; a sixth TL;DR example and four standup instructions followed when later reviews read the lane documents whole. - §1, §3, §5 and §6 are not edited. - 2026-09-15 · v1 · **User-confirmed** (NN-6), after TASK-262 rounds 4a and 4b retired a `BOARD.md` a project still holds: - §6 NN-2 takes the wording proposed in `perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-262-round3-result.md § 5`: no command reads, renders or creates a board file; a held file is read only by the import verbs, and every tool that sees one says it can be deleted. # Architecture — Perry > Written by: agent · Confirmed by: user (§1, §3 Forbidden, §5 versions, §6, §7) > Version: v1 > Last reviewed: 2026-09-15 > Hard cap: ≤ 500 lines. It has two readers — the user in one sitting, and every > agent that is dispatched against it — and the second one pays for it per turn. > Overflow → split per-§ to `architecture/sections/§-.md`. **This file existing is what makes it binding.** There is no draft state: a document that describes the system is the description, and a change that contradicts a section stops and asks the user (DESIGN-017 decisions 2 and 4). ## §1. Mission & scope Perry is a project office for solo and small projects, run by agents and read by one human. It keeps goals, work and decisions as files in the project's own repository, and it computes every number it reports rather than eyeballing it. It runs as a **skill** on three hosts — Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex CLI — with no install step and no service. The `bin/` tools are stdlib-only Python 3 and POSIX-ish bash, invoked by the skill's own procedures. It deliberately does **not**: run unattended (every write is a command an agent was asked to make), judge what a document means in code (that is an agent's job, `DESIGN-014`), or hold state outside the project it is pointed at (`ADR-002` — there is no cross-project registry). ## §2. Components ### `bin/` — the deterministic tools - **Purpose**: read and write project state. Twenty-one executables plus three shared libraries; `perry-kernel` is the `kernel/` CLI below. - **Owns**: every write to a canonical store, every computed number the standup prints, the argument contract those calls are made through, and the **next-step recommendation**: `perry-state --section next` evaluates the declared rule table `reference/next-rules.json` over the payload it already computes, so the same state gives the same recommendation. The move is the user's decision, `perry/design/DESIGN-020-guided-planning.md § 9`, the 2026-09-15 entry, confirmed by the user in session. - **Doesn't own**: the rules, which are declared in `reference/`, or the procedure around a recommendation — when to show it and what to ask the user are the `SKILL.md` files'. These tools execute, compute and refuse. - **Module document**: [`bin/ARCHITECTURE.md`](bin/ARCHITECTURE.md) ### `kernel/` — the PMO kernel (DESIGN-023) - **Purpose**: hold a project's structured state in one store per project anchor and answer for it through one CLI, JSON in and JSON out. Built by DESIGN-023 § 6 row B, behind `bin/perry-kernel`; `bin/` stays the live writer until each lane cuts over. - **Owns**: the store (`/perry/.db`, or `/.perry/perry.db` outside git) and its deterministic export under `/export/`; eight concepts and at most twelve command groups; every structural check a guard can decide without reading for meaning; and the derived fields `startable`, `blocked_by`, a metric's `met` and `fraction`, and `rollup`. - **Doesn't own**: the method. Item types, states, fields and guards are the process template, which the skill ships as data under `templates/process/`. The kernel reads no markdown, runs no command, and names no skill path or template-declared name. - **Module document**: [`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md`](kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md) ### `release/` — Perry product versions and releases - **Purpose**: maintain Perry's own product versions and verified release updates. - **Owns**: typed release records, deterministic VERSION/CHANGELOG projections, integration checks and explicit publication of an exact tested commit. - **Doesn't own**: the versions or state of projects managed by Perry, the meaning of authored change notes, or the user's decision to raise a major version. - **Procedure**: [`release/README.md`](release/README.md). ### `viewer/parsers.py` — the one reader - **Purpose**: parse every state file. 5,228 lines, one implementation. - **Owns**: `OKR.md`, phase, linkage, config and architecture parsing, and the store readers the read payloads answer from — a `BOARD.md` a project still holds is parsed only for the import verbs (TASK-262 round 4b); the project-root and state-root resolution, and the `installed` predicate, both `bin/` and the skill read through. - **Doesn't own**: writing. A second parser is the defect this repository has shipped twice; `NN-1` below is that rule. ### `schema/` — the declared shape - **Purpose**: `state-schema.json` (107KB) declares every file, heading, table, enum, store and claim. Eight contract pages publish the payloads outside consumers read; `next-contract.md` is the eighth. - **Owns**: what a file must look like, and what a payload promises. - **Doesn't own**: how a tool reaches that shape. ### `SKILL.md` + `goals/` `work/` `decide/` — the lanes - **Purpose**: the router (tier 0, read on every invocation; its byte cap is `tests/test_router_budget.py`'s) and three lane files loaded on demand. - **Owns**: procedure — what an agent does, in what order, and when it stops to ask the user. A lane **renders** the next step `perry-state --section next` returns: **in a standup's TL;DR and in its next-step position** it does not add, drop or reorder a recommendation, and it may add one line marked as its own note (`perry/design/DESIGN-020-guided-planning.md § 9`, the 2026-09-15 entry, confirmed by the user in session). - **Outside that rule**, and still the lane's own to write: a procedural step inside a subcommand's instructions ("read this, then run that"); the remediation a refusal names ("no current phase — run `plan-phase` first"); bootstrap and first-run prompts; and a hint in a rendered dashboard row. First-time setup is the largest of them: on a directory with no Perry state `R-setup` recommends only `/perry`, and the order setup recommends after that is the router's own (`reference/first-run.md § The recommended order for a new project`, which the router's first-time setup points to). The rule is about the one position the next block owns, not about naming a command. - **Doesn't own**: any number, or which step to recommend. Every figure a lane prints comes from a `bin/` call, and so does the recommendation. ### `modes/`, `packs/`, `reference/`, `templates/` - **Purpose**: the domain pack (`software-ops`), tier-1 reference pages loaded on demand, document scaffolds, and `templates/process/` JSON applied through the kernel. The legacy mode pages remain until final disposal; the work lane no longer runs stage, WIP, SLA or cadence procedures. `reference/` also holds `next-rules.json`, the rule table `bin/perry-state` evaluates for the next step, and `next.md`, which explains each rule. - **Owns**: process template data, retained legacy mode vocabulary, pack glossaries and legacy next-step rules, declared as data that `bin/` evaluates. ### `tests/` — 166 modules - **Purpose**: the contract, executable. Includes `tests/tree_guard.py`, which fails the suite if a run changed the checkout it ran in. - **Owns**: whether a claim in this repository is true. ### `perry/` and `.perry/` — this project's own state - **Purpose**: Perry's state root and anchor. Perry runs its own office in its own repository. ## §3. Boundaries & dependencies ```mermaid flowchart TD User([the one human]) -->|reads, decides| Lanes Lanes["SKILL.md · goals / work / decide
procedure only"] -->|invokes| Bin Bin["bin/ — 23 tools
compute and write"] -->|imports| Parsers["viewer/parsers.py
the one reader"] Bin -->|imports| Lib["bin/lib · perry_store · perry_md_store"] Bin -->|validates against| Schema["schema/state-schema.json"] Parsers -->|reads| State[("perry/ · .perry/
stores and projections")] Bin -->|writes| State Tests["tests/ — 166 modules"] -.asserts.-> Bin Tests -.asserts.-> Parsers Tests -.asserts.-> Schema Outside([aiMark and other consumers]) -->|published payloads| Contracts["schema/*-contract.md"] Contracts -.described by.-> Bin ``` Allowed directions: lanes → tools → libraries → state. Tools import `parsers`; `parsers` imports nothing from `bin/`. Forbidden, and each one has cost this project something: - **A second reader of any state file.** `bin/` never re-implements a parse. - **A lane computing a number.** If a figure is not in a payload, the tool grows the field; the procedure does not count rows. - **A tool reaching another project.** Roots come from `--root`, then `$PERRY_PROJECT`, then the walk up — `ADR-002`, and `bin/lib § resolve_project_root` is the one implementation. **Sunset (proposed, DESIGN-023)**: this becomes false at DESIGN-023 § 6 row H. The kernel's resolver (`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.7, NN-K5) is the second implementation DESIGN-023 introduces. It walks in the same order as `bin/lib § resolve_project_root` with a different predicate — it stops at the first `.perry/`, not the first installed project — and it refuses (`anchor_not_found`) where `bin/lib` falls back to the working directory or takes a `--root` or `$PERRY_PROJECT` that holds no `.perry/`. `kernel/tests/test_resolver_agreement.py` pins those four differences on both sides and shows the two agree on a shared set of fixture roots. The copies that already exist are unchanged and go at row H: `bin/perry-state § resolve_root`, `viewer/parsers.py § _resolve_project_root`, the flag/env/cwd lines in `perry-decide`, `perry-task`, `perry-knowledge`, `perry-state-cost`, `perry-context-budget` and `perry-explain`, `bin/perry-churn § detect_perry`, which walks up to the first `.perry/`, stops at the git top level, and takes no `--root` and no environment variable, and `perry-lint`, which reads no `$PERRY_PROJECT` at any of its nine sites: one, the default lint, walks, and eight per-mode branches (`--claims`, `--verification`, `--summaries`, `--glossary`, `--reviews`, `--knowledge`, `--provenance`, `--specs`) take `--root` or else the cwd, with no walk. - **An agent writing `ARCHITECTURE.md`.** This file is the user's. ## §4. Data flow **The store is truth; the markdown is a projection of it** (`ADR-007`). Every mutating command writes the record first. The board is not a file: `perry-tasks board` prints it from the stores. A `BOARD.md` a project still holds is retired — no write or reader uses it, only the `--from-board` imports read it, and every tool that sees it says to import and then delete it (TASK-262 rounds 4a and 4b). ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph write["a mutating command"] direction TB A["perry-task <verb>"] --> B["tasks.jsonl
the record"] B --> C["journal/<YYYY-MM>/<day>.md
the history line"] B --> E[".perry/events.jsonl
derived, disposable"] end B -.->|"(1) and (2) are one
recoverable transaction"| C C -.->|"(3) may fail alone
— reported, not silent"| E ``` Eight stores exist, one verdict line each in `perry-lint`'s census: `tasks.jsonl`, `risks.jsonl`, `intake.jsonl`, `asks.jsonl`, `cadence.jsonl`, `okr.jsonl`, `linkage.jsonl`, `.perry/config.jsonl`. `cadence.jsonl` is the newest (TASK-237 deliverable 3b). The read path is the mirror image and has one entry point: ```mermaid flowchart LR State[("stores + projections")] --> P["viewer/parsers.py"] P --> S["perry-state"] S -->|"--compact ≈ 11KB"| Standup["the standup, every session"] S -->|"--section <name>"| Detail["one key, in full"] S -->|"--section next --lane / --after"| Next["the next block,
narrowed"] S -->|"--json ≈ 174KB"| Whole["the whole payload"] T["perry-task list --json"] -->|"contract 2.4, bounded"| Outside([aiMark]) ``` `--section next` is the one section that is not always the payload's key as it stands. With `--lane` or `--after` it prints the block evaluated again over only that lane's or that subcommand's rules, plus the overlays (TASK-442). ## §5. Contracts ### Contract: `bin/` → an agent (the argument surface) - **Input**: ` [flags]`. Each tool declares its surface in `SURFACE`; the parser is driven by that declaration. - **Output**: exit 0 read or written · 1 refused, reason printed · 2 bad invocation · 3 the bytes match and the store did not produce them. These two bullets describe the other `bin/` tools: `bin/perry-kernel` has no `SURFACE` (`describe` is its surface), and its exit 3 is an internal fault (`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.1). - **Invariant on the tool**: a flag reaches only the subcommands that declare it. Accepted-and-dropped is a defect (`DESIGN-016` goal 12). - **Invariant on the caller**: a refusal is an outcome, not a failure. Do not fall back to editing the file by hand. ### Contract: `perry-task list --json` → outside consumers - `schema/task-list-contract.md`, version **2.4** (confirmed by the user 2026-09-15; 2.2 adds `installed`, 2.3 narrows it to a store with `.perry/` beside it, 2.4 reads no `BOARD.md` a project still holds — TASK-262 round 4b). `tasks[]` is bounded at 200 rows by default; `bound.open_total` carries the project's figure. - **Error mode**: a refusal is JSON on stdout, not prose on stderr. ### Contract: `perry-state --json` / `--compact` → the standup - `--compact` is a strict projection of `--json`, declared once in `perry-state § COMPACT` and asserted against the full payload by test. ### Contract: the schema → both sides - `perry-lint --templates` fails when a shipped template drifts from `state-schema.json`. That check is what keeps the standup from breaking silently. ## §6. Non-negotiables ### NN-1 — One reader per state file - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: exactly one implementation parses any given state file, and it lives in `viewer/parsers.py`. A `bin/` tool that needs a fact imports it. - **Rationale**: two parsers of `BOARD.md` disagreed in production twice, and the disagreement was invisible until a round-trip test one project later. - **Check**: `grep -rn "def parse_" bin/ | grep -v perry_store | grep -v _md_store` - **Known exceptions**: - `bin/perry-context-budget` reads one key (`session_context_ceiling`) of `.perry/config.jsonl` directly, because it must work outside a Perry project (USER-971, 2026-09-18). - `release/manage.py` reads `phase/CURRENT` at two git refs with its own "no phase" set: the pointer reader in `viewer/parsers.py` serves a working tree, and `release/` does not import `viewer/` (USER-981, 2026-09-21). - **Sunset (proposed, DESIGN-023)**: becomes false at DESIGN-023 § 6 row H, when `bin/`, the state readers in `viewer/parsers.py` and the state files they read are deleted, and structured state lives only in the kernel's store, read and written through the kernel CLI. Until row H it holds for everything `bin/` still reads. Its successor is `kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 3: nothing but the kernel opens the store, and only `export`, to decide `unchanged`, and `import` read the export. ### NN-2 — The store is truth; the projection is rendered - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: a mutating command writes the record first. Every reading of it — a payload and `perry-tasks board` — is derived from the record. No command reads, renders or creates a board file; a `BOARD.md` a project still holds is retired, is read only by the import verbs that upgrade the project, and every tool that sees one says it can be deleted. A projection edited by hand is not absorbed: the store is what every reading reports. - **Rationale**: `ADR-007`. Absorbing a hand edit destroys the canonical value; overwriting it destroys the human's intent. Both must be visible. - **Sunset (proposed, DESIGN-023)**: becomes false at DESIGN-023 § 6 row H, when `perry-tasks board`, the `BOARD.md` import verbs and every projection are deleted with `bin/`. The store stays the truth, and nothing is projected from it: readings come from kernel `query`, and the only file derived from the store is the export, which only `export`, to decide `unchanged`, and `import` read (`kernel/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.8). ### NN-3 — A write that cannot do what it claims refuses - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: no command reports a write it did not perform. A render that cannot place every stored record exits non-zero and names what it could not place. - **Rationale**: `DESIGN-016 § 1.5`. The documented recovery command reported `rendered … from 399 stored record(s)`, exit 0, having restored none of 151 deleted rows. ### NN-4 — Deterministic tools decide nothing about meaning - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: `bin/` makes only mechanical judgements. Whether a summary reads like prose, whether a spec's scope is adequate, whether an ADR applies — all belong to an agent or the user. - **Rationale**: `DESIGN-014`. Five rounds of regex lost to a full stop. - **Known exceptions**: `perry-codex-preflight` shells out to `codex exec` to check the CLI is alive. It judges nothing; it pings. ### NN-5 — The suite never writes into the tree it runs in - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: every test writes to a temporary root. `tests/tree_guard.py` runs on every exit path and fails the suite otherwise. - **Rationale**: an un-rooted `perry-task` call once discharged real board rows on every run for months, invisibly, because the sweep is idempotent. ### NN-6 — An agent may describe this file, and may not decide it - **Severity**: hard - **Rule**: an agent writes and rewrites the descriptive sections (§2, §4, §5's shapes, §8) freely. Changing §1, a `Forbidden` line in §3, a contract version in §5, or a confirmed rule in §6 is a question for the user, asked before the change lands. - **Rationale**: the agent doing the typing is what makes this document affordable, and the agent being unable to overrule it is what keeps it from becoming a mirror. The rule the directory exists to enforce: **a number Perry reports must be computed, never eyeballed.** An agent that reads `perry-tasks board` and counts blocked rows is right most of the time, and the times it is wrong are invisible. It decides one thing about what to do, and only from a declared table: `perry-state --section next` evaluates `reference/next-rules.json` over the payload it computes and returns the next-step recommendation that the lanes render. 22 · store ↔ projection, 5 registers · board"] Okr["perry-okr"] Goals["perry-goals"] Config["perry-config"] Decide["perry-decide"] Know["perry-knowledge"] end subgraph read["readers"] Task["perry-task
31 retained verbs · writes refused"] State["perry-state
the standup payload · the next block"] Lint["perry-lint
9 modes · the census"] Diag["perry-diagnose"] Explain["perry-explain"] Others["churn · state-cost · restore-check
context-budget · dispatch-limit
detect-host · update-check"] end subgraph index["the index"] Perry["perry
list · describe · forward"] end subgraph kernelcli["the kernel's CLI — no SURFACE, no bin/lib"] Kernel["perry-kernel

It and `perry-kernel-migrate` (below) are the two `bin/` tools that execute another tool. Each runs it as a subprocess and imports nothing from it: this one runs `perry-detect-host`, and the importer runs `perry-kernel` and `perry-task`. ### What `perry-kernel-migrate` runs and writes DESIGN-023 row D's importer (TASK-489). # Architecture — `kernel/` > Written by: agent · Confirmed by: — > Version: v1 > Last reviewed: 2026-10-07 > Module document for the `kernel/` component. [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../ARCHITECTURE.md) § 2 names it; the user confirmed that entry on 2026-09-24 (merged in 34d7be63). > Cap: ≤ 600 lines. This is the kernel's specification, written before any kernel code exists (DESIGN-023 § 6 row A). The design it specifies is `perry/design/DESIGN-023-a-kernel-and-a-skill.md`. > Overflow → split per-§ to `architecture/sections/§-.md`, the root document's convention under `kernel/`. § 5 is split out. ## §1. Mission & scope The kernel holds a project's structured state and applies the structural rules that a process template declares. It is stdlib-only Python behind one CLI, and every command takes JSON and returns JSON. The skill (markdown) calls the kernel. The kernel never calls the skill. The kernel knows eight concepts (§ 2) and no method. Every item type, state, field, transition and guard comes from the template, which is data that the skill ships. The names in this document's examples (`widget`, `gauge`, `queued`, `bench`, `inspector`) are invented and mean nothing to the kernel. DESIGN-023 Goal 1 applies to this document as it does to the code. It deliberately does **not** read, parse, lint or render markdown (Goal 2). It does not run a command or spawn a process (decision 8), judge what a document means (decision 3), or recommend a next step (decision 5). It does not serve several users, run a server, sync machines or draw a UI (§ 3 Non-Goals). Status: built by DESIGN-023 § 6 row B; `bin/` stays the live writer until each lane cuts over, and row C writes the first template. ## §2. Components ### The eight concepts (Goal 6) | Concept | Fields | |---|---| | **Template** | `format` (the kernel's template-format version, `1`), `name`, `version` (a positive integer that only rises), `types{}`, `relations{}`. One version is applied at a time, and applying one is an event (§ 5.2) | | **Item** | `id` (minted from its type's prefix), `type`, `state`, `fields{}` (every declared field, `null` when unset), `seq` (the seq of the last event that touched it), `created_at`, `updated_at` | | **Field** | declared per type: `kind` is one of `text` `int` `number` `date` `enum` `actor` `ref` `list` `metric`, plus that kind's options (§ 5.3). Its value lives on the item | | **Transition** | declared per type: `name`, `from` (one or more states), `to` (one state), `guards[]` | | **Guard** | `kind` (`required` · `actor` · `relations_closed` · `limit`), the kind's keys, and an optional `when` (§ 5.4). Guards run on create and on transitions | | **Relation** | `kind`, `from`, `to`. The built-in kinds are `blocks` (*from* blocks *to*) and `parent` (*to* is the parent of *from*). The template can declare others | | **Event** | `seq`, `at`, `actor`, `command`, `items[]`, `transition`, `changes[]` (each with a `key` and its `before` and `after` values), `note`, `warnings[]`. Events are append-only and are the store's history (ADR-022) | | **Attachment** | `item`, `ref` (a path or URL, kept verbatim), `hash` (optional, `sha256:`). The kernel never opens the target | `startable`, `blocked_by`, a metric's `met` and `fraction`, and an item's `rollup` are derived when read and never stored (§ 5.5, § 5.6). ### Layout (DESIGN-023 § 5.5) `kernel/` holds the `perry_kernel` package, its tests and this file. The executable, `bin/perry-kernel`, is a thin wrapper of a few lines that imports `perry_kernel` and calls its `main()`; the user named it on 2026-09-24 (OQ-K6), and row H renames it `bin/perry`. The package is cached as bytecode, so nothing is recompiled per call. This document writes `kernel`. ### The budget **8 concepts** (the eight above) and **at most 12 command groups**. Ten groups are in use: `init`, `template`, `item`, `rel`, `attach`, `query`, `events`, `export`, `import` and `describe`. There are also **exactly 4 guard kinds and 9 field kinds**. A fifth guard kind or a tenth field kind is a concept change (DESIGN-023 § 3, § 7). **How a test checks it.** `describe` reports `concepts`, `budget` (`{"concepts": 8, "command_groups": 12}`), every command, and the template format's `field_kinds` and `guard_kinds`. The kernel suite asserts that `concepts` is exactly the list above, that `commands[].name` has at most 12 distinct first words, that there are 4 guard kinds and 9 field kinds, and that `budget` equals the test's own literals, 8 and 12. The test does not read this file, because the kernel suite must pass with every `*.md` removed (Goal 2). Raising a number means editing both the test literal and this section, and DESIGN-023 § 7 makes that a revision of the design, not a new row. ## §3. Boundaries & dependencies ```mermaid flowchart TD Skill["skill — SKILL.md, lanes, templates/process/*.json
markdown and data"] -->|"argv + JSON in"| CLI["kernel executable
thin wrapper"] Migrate["bin/perry-kernel-migrate
row D's one-shot importer, deleted at row H"] -->|"subprocess: argv + JSON in
--store and --root always named"| CLI CLI -->|imports| Pkg["perry_kernel
stdlib only"] Pkg -->|"sqlite3, WAL"| Store[("store
<git-common-dir>/perry/<slug>.db")] Pkg -->|"export writes and compares · import loads"| Export[("<state root>/export/
items.jsonl · events.jsonl")] Pkg -.->|"reads .git and commondir
for the path rule"| Git[(".git metadata")] CLI -->|"JSON out"| Skill CLI -->|"JSON out"| Migrate ``` Besides the skill, `bin/perry-kernel-migrate`, DESIGN-023 § 6 row D's one-shot importer (TASK-489), calls the CLI until row H deletes it. It runs the CLI as a subprocess, with `--store` and `--root` always named and `PERRY_KERNEL_TESTING` set (§ 5.7). It imports nothing from `perry_kernel`, and it reaches the store only through the CLI, as the skill does (`bin/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 2). The test suites also run the CLI, and `bin/perry` forwards `perry kernel …` to the wrapper's `main` in-process. Allowed directions: skill → kernel → store, where each caller named above stands in the skill's place. There are no others. Forbidden: - **Importing anything outside the stdlib and `perry_kernel`**, `bin/`, `viewer/` and `release/` included. **Reading markdown**, in any mode (the suite runs with no `*.md`). - **Running a command.** The kernel makes no `subprocess`, `os.system`, `os.exec*` or `os.spawn*` call. It finds the git common dir by reading `.git` and `commondir` (§ 5.7). The skill runs a measurement's command and writes the value (decision 8). - **Naming a skill path or a template-declared name.** Goal 1's test greps the kernel source for every type, state and field name in the shipped template as a string literal (`"name"` or `'name'`), case-sensitively. A collision is fixed by renaming on the kernel's side. - **Any other path.** The kernel reads only its store, its `--input` file, the `.git` metadata and the export. It writes only the store and `/export/`. Only `import` loads the export; `export` reads its own files only to tell `unchanged` apart. ## §4.
